reason: The text demonstrates agency among non-leaders as well as leaders. The Israelite people (non-leaders) exercise agency by multiplying ('וַיִּשְׁרְצ֛וּ וַיִּרְבּ֥וּ'), crying out to God ('וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ'), and their cry ascends to God ('וַתַּ֧עַל שַׁוְעָתָ֛ם אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים'), which triggers divine response. Additionally, Egyptian magicians/wise men (not supreme leaders) perform signs ('חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּלַהֲטֵיהֶ֖ם'). While Moses, Aaron, and Pharaoh as leaders possess significant agency, the text portrays agency as distributed across multiple social strata.
